answer: Each identity posts an 80-credit departure bond on the basalt ledger at inlet entry, plus a 15-credit fee, locked until closure. To leave, it presents an inlet-to-exit record, and an onyx auditor replays it: all fees, deliveries, and payments must match, or the bond burns and exit is refused. One bond settles one key, so a rented exit record fails the key check and burns both bonds. The k-th fake still pays the full 95 credits, with no bulk discount, so 1,000 fakes put 95,000 credits at risk. Ghost-exit rings forfeit every bond. Honest identities pay 15 once and recover the bond.
